text.content:
The level-1 Human

Humanity            [TRAIT Human][SIZE Medium][SPEED 6][VIGOR 8]
                    [EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, aid; IF: RANK(Origin >= trained)]
Driven              [POINT Calling]
Quick Study         [POINT Skill]
Stubborn Footing    [EFFECT IMMUNE: prone; LIMIT: encounter]
Close Ranks         [EFFECT DEF: 1 situation, guard; IFT: BLOW; FOR: self+allies 0; IF: ALLIES(>=1, 0)]
Versatile Human     [POINT Opening]
Jack of All Trades  [EFFECT CHECK: 1 situation; IF: RANK(roll = untrained)]
Torchbearer Human   [AURA 15 allies; DEF: 1 situation; IF: SEEN; IFT: TRAIT(Fear); LIMIT: round]
Steady the Line     [MANEUVER Steady the Line]          Effect: @Maneuver[Steady the Line]

Close Ranks in words: FOR: self+allies 0 is who gets the bonus; IF: ALLIES(>=1, 0) is the owner's condition. An ally receives it only while within 0 ft of the owner, which is the same adjacency, so one line serves both halves of "both of you". Torchbearer Human is the Rally Aura (Mike's text of 2026-11-05: "The first time each round an ally within 15 feet who can see you defends against an Attack with the Fear trait, they gain a +1 Situation bonus to that Defense check"): one block draws the ring and gives every Defense of an ally within it who can see the owner a +1 against an attack carrying Fear, once a round per ally.

The two Cultures

Serrovanian         [LANGUAGE Common, Serrovine]
                    [EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, diplomacy; IF: CLAIM(toward someone who shares your Culture)]
Oathbound           [MANEUVER Oathbound]                 Effect: @Maneuver[Oathbound]
Contract Literate   [EFFECT CHECK: 2 condition; IF: CLAIM(noticing hidden clauses, traps or altered terms in an agreement)]
Iron Etiquette      [EFFECT DEF: 1 condition; IFT: CHECK(intimidation)]
                    [EFFECT DEF: 1 condition; IF: CLAIM(against a social manipulation other than Intimidation)]
Reacher             [LANGUAGE Common, Reachspeak]
                    [EFFECT CHECK: 1 condition, diplomacy; IF: CLAIM(toward someone who shares your Culture)]
Quick Tongue        [MANEUVER Quick Tongue]              Effect: @Maneuver[Quick Tongue]
Riverfoot           [EFFECT IGNORE: terrain, mud, decking, loose stone, shallow water]
                    [EFFECT SPEED: 1 situation; LIMIT: encounter]
Broker's Eye        [EFFECT CHECK: 2 situation, diplomacy; IF: CLAIM(when trading)]
                    [EFFECT CHECK: 2 situation, guile; IF: CLAIM(when trading)]

The Backgrounds and the Callings

Acrobat             [Acrobatics trained][Athletics trained][Lore trained]
Soldier             [Athletics trained][Intimidation trained][Lore trained]
Criminal            [Guile trained][Stealth trained][Lore trained]
Weaponmaster Calling   [Athletics trained][CHOICE Weapon Group][TALENT Weapon Familiarity][VIGOR opening 10]
Berserker Calling      [Athletics trained][VIGOR opening 12]
(every other Calling Root: its Trained Skill and its Opening Vigor the same way)

The Talent Maneuvers (the "Talent Maneuvers" sheet of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx)

Steady the Line  ❶↺   [EFFECT IMMUNE: expose; FOR: allies 0]
Oathbound        ❶    [EFFECT MARK: enemies]
                      [EFFECT ATK: 1 condition; IFT: MARKED]
                      [EFFECT DEF: 1 condition; IFT: MARKED]
Quick Tongue     ❶↺   [EFFECT REROLL: diplomacy; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]

Aid, and two Talents that change it (0.22.0)

Aid  ❶                [EFFECT GIVE: 2 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll <= expert)]
                      [EFFECT GIVE: 3 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll = master)]
                      [EFFECT GIVE: 4 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: RANK(roll = legendary)]
                      [EFFECT GIVE: 1 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(success)]
                      [EFFECT GIVE: -1 situation, chosen; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]
Patient Assistance    [EFFECT ALTER: Aid.beneficial-duration; VALUE: recipient opportunity 2]
Sure Assistance       [EFFECT ALTER: Aid.critical-failure; VALUE: nothing]

The five lines are Aid's row on the Basic Actions sheet of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx; the two Talents are the Human's. These cells are Mike's to paste: the 0.22.0 release carries the kinds, and both workbooks were in his hands when it was cut. What the system does not read of Aid, and the table does: its Threshold ("typically 15") and whether the help makes sense. (Its ❶ is paid when the roll is made since 0.23.0.)

Move Together, and the Talent that changes it (0.24.0)

Move Together  ❶      [EFFECT PERMIT: move; FOR: allies 0; LIMIT: round]
Coordinated Footwork  [EFFECT ALTER: Move Together.movement; VALUE: step]

The first line is Move Together's row on the Ancestry Actions sheet of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx; the second is the Human Talent's cell. Both are Mike's to paste: the 0.24.0 release carries the kind, and both workbooks were in his hands when it was cut. What the system does not read of Move Together, and the table does: that both routes are declared before either moves, that you move first, that the ally can perceive your cue, and that the ally is willing.

Pay It Forward, and the Talent that changes it (0.25.0)

Pay It Forward  ⓿     [EFFECT SUBORDINATE: Aid; IF: EFFECT(Aid, used); LIMIT: encounter]
Reciprocal Effort     [EFFECT ALTER: Pay It Forward.limit; VALUE: round]

The first line is Pay It Forward's row, which is not yet on the Ancestry Actions sheet of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx (its text is in Mike's draft workbook); the second is the Human Talent's cell. Both are Mike's to add: the 0.25.0 release carries the kind, and both workbooks were in his hands when it was cut. Pay It Forward needs Aid's own five GIVE lines above to be on Aid's row, since without them no Aid gives a result to use up. What the system does not read of Pay It Forward, and the table does: that the ally is willing, and that Aid's own requirements are met.

What the system does not read, and the table does: whom Oathbound may name ("a creature that has either formally challenged you, or that has broken a bargain or a truce with you"; the mark takes the targeted enemy); Quick Tongue's Requirements (a settlement, and not used there within a month); Broker's Eye's "always know an item's fair price"; and which agreement, trade or social manipulation is in front of the player, which is what CLAIM asks them. Iron Etiquette's two lines are one Talent, so an Intimidation match and a ticked claim together are +1, not +2 (PHB v4.21's stacking collapses one source).

What each Maneuver needs (0.28.0)

The [REQUIRES ...] block for every row of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx whose Requirements, Target or Effect names something the system can check. They are Mike's to paste: the 0.28.0 release carries the kind, and the workbook was in his hands when it was cut. Each goes in the row's Automation cell, in place of an N/A or an empty cell, or on a line of its own beside the row's other blocks. Until a row has its block the Maneuvers tab always lists it.

Reading Effects (0.31.0)

And on a Talent or a Maneuver a character owns, a bonus that waits on an Effect:

  [EFFECT ATK: 1 situation; IFT: EFFECT(prone)]              +1 to attacks against a Prone creature
  [EFFECT DEF: 1 situation; IF: EFFECT(Taking Cover)]        +1 to Defenses while you have Taking Cover
  [EFFECT CHECK: 1 situation, intimidation; IFT: EFFECT(frightened)]   +1 to Intimidation against the Frightened

An Effect that is no Condition is put on by a Maneuver's APPLY line (below), or by hand: the plus beside "Active Effects" on the Effects tab of either sheet, then its name.

Putting Effects on (0.32.0)

What the rows of data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx say today, written with APPLY and REMOVE. They are for Mike to paste: no workbook was written. Each block goes on a line of its own in the row's Automation cell, beside any [REQUIRES ...] block the row has.

  Stand ❶          [REQUIRES prone or supine]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: prone]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: Supine]

  Drop Prone ⓿     [REQUIRES not prone]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: Supine]

  Drop Supine ⓿    [REQUIRES not supine]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: Supine]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: prone]
                   (0.32.1; Mike split Drop Prone in two rather than have a box ask which. Each row
                   takes the other state off, so a creature is never both, and Dropping Prone while
                   Supine turns it over)

  Take Cover ❶     [EFFECT APPLY: Taking Cover]
                   (its end, "until you Move, Step or Attack", is an event: take it off by hand)

  Trip ❶ to ❷      [EFFECT APPLY: prone, target; IF: RESULT(critical success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone, target; IF: RESULT(success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: off-guard; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(failure); IF: COST(2)]

  Shove ❶ to ❷     [EFFECT APPLY: off-guard; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(failure); IF: COST(2)]

  Disarm ❷ to ❸    [EFFECT APPLY: off-guard; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(failure); IF: COST(3)]

  Grapple          [EFFECT APPLY: restrained, target; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: grabbed, target; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone, target; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: COST(2)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone, target; IF: RESULT(success); IF: COST(2)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone; IF: RESULT(success); IF: COST(2)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: off-guard; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical failure); IF: COST(1)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: prone; IF: RESULT(critical failure); IF: COST(2)]
                   (its Cost cell reads 0 today; the COST lines wait for it to read "1 to 2")

  Demoralize       [EFFECT APPLY: frightened 2, target; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: COST(1)]
  ❶ to ❸           [EFFECT APPLY: frightened 1, target; IF: RESULT(success); IF: COST(1)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: frightened 3, target; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: COST(3)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: heedless, target; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical success); IF: COST(3)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: frightened 2, target; IF: RESULT(success); IF: COST(3)]
                   (❷ Break Them, many creatures at once, is by hand: a card has one target)

  Feint ❶          [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed, target; UNTIL: giver opportunity end; IF: RESULT(critical success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed, target; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(success)]
                   [EFFECT APPLY: wrong-footed; UNTIL: giver opportunity; IF: RESULT(critical failure)]

  Escape ❶ to ❷    [EFFECT REMOVE: grabbed; IF: RESULT(critical success)]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: restrained; IF: RESULT(critical success)]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: grabbed; IF: RESULT(success)]
                   [EFFECT REMOVE: restrained; IF: RESULT(success)]

And on a Talent, a line that reads what a Maneuver of yours put on a creature:

  [EFFECT ATK: 1 situation; IFT: EFFECT(wrong-footed, mine)]      +1 to attacks against a creature you Wrong-Footed
  [EFFECT DEF: 1 situation; IF: EFFECT(Taking Cover)]             +1 to Defenses while you have Taking Cover

What these rows say that a line cannot yet: "Wrong-Footed TO a creature" on yourself (the Condition goes on you; whom it is to is the table's), a window that ends with ANOTHER creature's Opportunity on an Effect that is on you (Tumble Through's Critical Failure), damage, pushes and movement, a result applied to each of several creatures (Hide, Sneak, Captivate), "its next Attack against you" (Talk Them Down, Anticipate, Bolster: a Basic row cannot carry the line that reads it), and a degree raised by an Exposed Zone (Trip's Special).

The Conditions (0.33.0)

The rows of data/conditions.xlsx that carry lines or count as another Condition, as the workbook was first filled (section 11 says how a row is read). Every other row is N/A.

  Condition      Takes  Includes               Automation
  Off-Guard                                    [EFFECT DEF: -2 situation, evade]
                                               [EFFECT DEF: -2 situation, guard]
  Frightened     N                             [EFFECT DEF: -N condition]
                                               [EFFECT CHECK: -N condition]
                                               [EFFECT ATK: -N condition]
  Fatigued       N                             [EFFECT DEF: -N condition]
                                               [EFFECT ATK: -N condition]
  Prone                 Off-Guard              [EFFECT ATK: -2 situation]
                                               [EFFECT DEF: 2 situation, evade; IFT: RANGED]
  Supine                Off-Guard              (the same two lines)
  Grabbed               Off-Guard              N/A
  Restrained            Grabbed                N/A
  Blind                 Off-Guard              N/A
  Unconscious           Prone                  N/A
  Wrong-Footed   X      Off-Guard against X    N/A

What these rows say that a line cannot yet: Supine's "except melee Attacks against adjacent creatures" (its -2 reaches those too), "cannot Move or Step", Evade being unavailable while Grabbed (the system marks that itself), a value that drops by 1 each round (Frightened, Slowed), Stunned's and Slowed's lost actions, Heedless's extra action, what Blind and Deafened cannot perceive, and Fatigued's maximum, Wind check and rests, which stay the system's.

The character sheet's Effects tab (0.16.0, the Overview's panel through 0.16.0; Mike: FG's "Character Effects field ... automated and shown on the Tracker, or on the Character sheet") lists every effect line the character carries, from Talents, Maneuvers and the custom effects below, each with its As read line. A line the system applies by itself has FG's three-state switch On / Skip / Off: Skip lets the next application pass and returns to On; Off silences the line until it is turned back on. A line the system cannot apply by itself, one with IF: CLAIM(...), has instead Apply to next roll (0.17.0): pressed, the bonus comes ticked in the next roll dialog or is applied to the next Threshold read, and the button goes out; the pin on the Talent's row is the same switch. Custom effects are lines the owner or the GM types on the sheet in the bare form, as FG's field takes them (ATK: 2 situation; LIMIT: round, DEF: 1 situation, guard; IF: CLAIM(behind the cart); the [EFFECT ...] wrapper reads there too), with a duration: until removed, the next roll, or the end of the encounter. They act exactly as a Talent's lines do. The combat tracker shows a badge with the count of a combatant's active effects and their summaries on hover. The Grammar button on the panel opens this document's journal.

A USE line (0.21.0) is a third case. The system neither applies it by itself nor waits for it to be armed: it offers the swap in the roll dialog, and the line has On / Skip / Off like any effect line. On: offered when the roll is made from the Maneuver the line names. Skip: left out of the next such roll, then back On (a roll that is not that Maneuver's does not spend the Skip). Off: never offered. On a roll with no dialog (a Shift-click) a swap that would come ticked is applied, so Skip and Off are the ways to decline it there. A custom effect may be a USE line too (USE: Presence, Origin, aid), with the same three durations; one that lasts the next roll leaves only when its swap is the one rolled.

Pending results (0.22.0) are a list of their own on the tab, under the effect lines: what another character's Maneuver has given this one and it has not yet used ("Aid from Tess: +1 Situation bonus to the next Crafting roll, until Tess's next Opportunity"). A pending result has no switch. The next roll with its Constellation uses it, its window closes it, and the bin beside it is the GM's alone: a player does not strike a penalty a failed Aid left. It counts in the tab's total and in the tracker's badge. A GIVE line on a copy of a Maneuver the character owns, and an ALTER line on a Talent, are effect lines like any other and have On / Skip / Off; an ALTER may be a custom effect too (ALTER: Aid.critical-failure; VALUE: nothing). A GIVE may not: it is written on the Maneuver's row.

pages.name: What a rule does in play, and what it does not

text.content:
• A bonus to a Constellation moves its Threshold. A Defense's Threshold is 10 plus the same modifiers its roll uses, so [EFFECT DEF: 1 situation, guard] raises the Guard Threshold on the sheet, in the Combat Prompt's preview and on the attack card, and the Guard roll alike. A Skill's Threshold, wherever one is shown (the party's Skills grid, the Relevant Check picker), is 10 plus the check's own modifier, so it moves too. Both of the player's paths are covered: a player defending against an adversary's attack rolls their Defense, and the roll carries the bonus (and writes the LIMIT mark); a player attacking a player rolls against the defender's Threshold (one die for each defender since 0.26.0), and the Threshold the coordinator reads carries it. A rule that needs the attack (IFT: Threats, IFT: TRAIT, IFT: CHECK), the map (FOR reaching others, ALLIES(...), SEEN), the other party (IFT: MARKED) or the round (LIMIT) is read at those moments and nowhere they are unknown.
  • Position is read where a token is known. The sheet's Defense Threshold is computed without the map, so it does not include such bonuses; its tooltip lists the rules it leaves out; the Combat Prompt's preview, the attack card's Threshold and every roll made with a token on the scene do include them.
  • **LIMIT: round and LIMIT: encounter are remembered on the recipient** (a flag on the Actor, flags.starwrought.rules.round or .encounter, keyed by the Talent and the line, naming the Combat and the round). The client that resolves the roll writes the mark: the coordinator's client for an attack read against a Threshold, the roller's for a Defense roll or a check; a preview writes nothing. A client that may not write the recipient (a player's Defense roll spending a Skip on another player's Torchbearer line; an attacker's roll reading a body it does not own) hands the mark over the system socket to the GM's client, else to an active owner's (0.18.1); only a table with neither sees the rule apply again.
  • A claim is the player's decision, at the roll (ruling 174). A CLAIM bonus is a checkbox in the roll dialog, unticked, hint and all; ticked, it joins the roll and prints on the card by the Talent's name. Apply to next roll (the Effects tab) and the pin on the Talent's row arm it for the next roll (the box comes ticked) or the next Threshold read (applied, since no dialog shows); both go out when either resolves. Nothing is applied unasked, and nothing is remembered past that one roll.
  • The other party is read per pairing (ruling 175). A Defense roll and a Threshold read know the attacker; a Strike's blind die knows nobody (it is thrown before any Threshold is read; one for each defender since 0.26.0, where through 0.25.0 one die was read against them all), so a rule about the defender (IFT: MARKED) is read as each pairing resolves and added to that pairing's total, listed on its card and kept for a reroll of it. Each of those dice is its own roll: the attacker's own LIMIT: line, a pending result an ally gave and an armed claim are used by the first die and are gone for the next, and the dice are thrown one at a time so that holds. Outside an encounter a LIMIT: round line has no round to count and every die carries it. A Strike with no target rolls against a typed Threshold and has no other party.
  • A mark names one creature (ruling 176). flags.starwrought.rules.marks.<carrier> on the owner: the targeted token, its name and the Combat it was made in. It holds while that Combat is the viewed one; made outside an encounter it holds until the next encounter starts or the Maneuver is used again. Using the Maneuver asks for exactly one target of the kind MARK names.
  • A reroll pays once, in an encounter (ruling 177). The button on the card pays the carrier's cost through the owner's actions when a Combat is running and charges nothing outside one; the new card names the Talent and says its Requirements are the table's.
  • A check against a Threshold reads it live (ruling 179). A Maneuver whose check names a Defense (Demoralize against Guard), used with one target, reads that target's Threshold through the same fold the attack flow uses (the Threat check and the attacker known, so IFT: CHECK(...) and IFT: MARKED apply), prints the number for a character target or a GM roller, and withholds an adversary's as the flow does.
  • Terrain is on the map (ruling 178). A Difficult terrain region behavior carries a kind and a multiplier; [EFFECT IGNORE: terrain, <kind>] makes the owner's token cross that kind as open ground. A region the GM hides carries no terrain for anyone (Foundry's rule), so a terrain region is never hidden to keep it secret; players toggle their own overlay instead.
  • **A prevent of a Condition refuses the write wherever the system sets the Condition (Drop Flat at the reveal, the final Legs Wound, the token palette, the Effects tab) and posts one card saying which Talent prevented it. A prevent of expose is answered on the resolution card: the Expose widget shows the Reaction's button for each ally whose Maneuver reaches the attacker; pressed, the ally's cost is paid, the card says "It Exposes nothing", and the Expose widget is gone. Pressed after the Zone was picked** it closes the Zone this card Exposed, and the card says so (ruling 172). A Zone Exposed by anything but this card is never touched.
  • A Talent Maneuver ([MANEUVER X]) is an owned action Item copied from the Actions pack when the Talent lands (a drag onto the sheet, the wizard, or the GM's ready pass after Sync content), flagged with the Talent that granted it, listed under "From your Talents", and deleted with the Talent. Its cost is the row's Cost column; its rules are the row's Automation, indexed on the character as any owned Item's are.
  • An aura is a preview until shown (0.17.0). [AURA ...] draws on hover, on selection and while the token is dragged; the Auras window on the token's HUD shows a ring to everyone for the encounter, and that choice is the character's (system.auras.visible), not the cell's.
  • A substitution swaps two terms, at the roll, when the player lets it (0.21.0; rulings 216 to 220; section 4, substitute). A USE line is offered in the roll dialog of a check made from the Maneuver's own Item, ticked when the swapped total is strictly higher, one swap to a roll. It replaces the Attribute Bonus and the Proficiency Bonus and nothing else, the card names both pairs, and the rank the roll records is the rank rolled. Never a Strike, a Cast, a Defense roll, a Threshold read or an Initiative, and never an adversary's roll.
  • A rule about the roll's rank reads the rank rolled (ruling 217). A line such as Jack of All Trades' IF: RANK(roll = untrained) does not hold on a roll whose swap borrows a Trained Proficiency Bonus (Mike's Talent text: the +1 "does not apply to ... a check receiving a substituted proficiency bonus"). That is why "better" is judged on the whole total: the swap is priced with the +1 gone, and the check as it was with the +1 in.
  • A bonus to a Maneuver follows the Maneuver onto a Defense's check (ruling 222). A check rolled with a Defense Constellation from that Maneuver's Item (an Aid made with Awareness) carries a bonus to the Maneuver (Humanity's +1 to Aid), which it lost through 0.20.1. Whether a bonus to every check reaches a Defense rolled as a check (Wind, Recovery, a Search) is untouched and is an open decision.
  • What a substitution does not read yet (0.21.0). Not built: a Constellation as the check a USE names (it brings the Initiative question of ruling 111 with the first Talent that wants it); offers on plain checks, made without the Maneuver's Item; IF: UNSUBSTITUTED; a flat Proficiency Bonus (Working Knowledge's "+3 instead of +0"); FOR and auras; CLAIM. Aid's own outcome is read since 0.22.0 (the next entries).
  • A Maneuver's result is given by a button, to one character, for one roll (0.22.0; rulings 226 and 227; section 4, give). The check's card carries the result of its degree; the giver's owner or the GM presses Give; the recipient holds one pending result of that Maneuver, which its next roll with the Constellation carries and removes. A check, a Maneuver's check, an attack, a Defense roll and an Initiative are rolls; the Threshold on the sheet and a Threshold read are not, so a pending bonus to Guard helps a Guard ROLL and never the number an attacker reads.
  • A window is counted on the result itself (ruling 228). Nothing in the system counts Opportunities, so a pending result remembers the Combat, the Combatant its window watches and how many of that fighter's Opportunities have begun. giver opportunity closes as the giver's next Opportunity begins; recipient opportunity 2 closes as the second of the recipient's upcoming Opportunities ends. The turn step a completed circuit of Passes takes on its way to the next round is nobody's Opportunity and is not counted. A lone fighter's step to itself, when nobody else has an action left, IS one: one Opportunity ended and the next began. Each character's window is settled by the GM's client, else by its own player's.
  • A change to what a Maneuver gives is read with the check (ruling 225; section 4, alter). The roller's ALTER lines are applied to the Maneuver's results when the check is made, and the card keeps the whole table, every degree at the rank rolled, so a reroll and a reload read the same answer. An ALTER never changes the roll or its degree.
  • What a give does not read yet (0.22.0). Not built: two uses of one result (Carry the Plan); a Condition given by a result; a result given by a Maneuver that rolls no check; an adversary as the recipient; the ALTER properties beyond the eight (a Maneuver's range, uses, slots); and a Threshold a Maneuver's check opens on (Aid's "typically 15"), which is still typed. With no GM connected the turn step that ends a round by Passes may be counted as an Opportunity by a player's client, and two presses of one card for two recipients owned by different players can both land. A GM stepping the turn backwards and forwards again counts an Opportunity twice, so a window of two Opportunities or more can close one early.
  • What a permit does not read (0.24.0). It permits a Move and nothing else. Not read, and the table's: that routes are declared first, the order of the two Moves, whether the cue can be perceived, whether the ally is willing. A mistaken use cannot be taken back, since the once-a-round mark stays for the round. A short Move forced by the Maneuver uses up a once-a-round Speed bonus as any Move does. A GM who repositions the permitted token during that Opportunity uses the permission and charges it. Each arrow-key nudge is its own movement, so the first nudge is the Maneuver's Move.
  • A subordinate Maneuver is its own use under its parent's name (0.25.0; rulings 245 and 246; section 4, subordinate). The parent row posts no card and pays nothing of its own: the cost, the limit and the used Effect are all settled when the subordinate's roll is made, so a closed dialog has spent nothing. The parent's cost is the only one paid.
  • A used Effect is left by the roll that used a bonus up, and lasts that Opportunity (ruling 247; section 3, Named Effect). It is written with the roll's own bookkeeping, by the roller's client or the one that writes for it, for a check, a Strike, a Cast and a Defense roll alike. It is taken off when its Opportunity ends (the turn moves on, forwards or back; a lone fighter steps to itself; the encounter ends) and when the Maneuver it triggers is used. The GM may bin it.
  • What a subordinate does not read (0.25.0). Not performed, and told so: a built-in, a Strike, a Cast or a movement row as the subordinate; a Prepared parent; two subordinates on one row; a subordinate chosen when the Maneuver is used (Shared Demonstration); one Aid check for several allies (Common Purpose, United Effort); Aid before an ally's roll (Timely Aid). Not read, and the table's: that the ally is willing, and that the subordinate's own requirements are met. A used Effect whose holder has no client connected to take it off when its Opportunity ends stays listed, dimmed, until the encounter ends; it is held for nothing by then. A roll made by the GM for a player's character leaves the Effect as that player's own roll would.
  • **A [REQUIRES ...] block decides what the Maneuvers tab lists, and nothing else (0.28.0; section 4). By default the tab shows only the Maneuvers that apply now; Show every Maneuver** at its top shows the rest dimmed, each with why on hover ("Needs: Prone or Supine"). A row is left out for four reasons: a block of its own that fails; in an encounter, an Exploration Activity or a Downtime Endeavor; in an encounter with the six-action round tracked, a cheapest cost above the actions left; and in an encounter outside the character's Opportunity with no approval of the GM's standing, anything but a Reaction. A Favorite (the bookmark on a row) is listed first and never left out. The list is worked out again when the character's Conditions, gear, Bind or actions change, when the Opportunity moves, when a token on the scene moves, when another creature's Conditions change, and when a wall or a door changes. Nothing is refused by it: a Maneuver shown with the button can be used. It is the character sheet's alone; an adversary's abilities are not filtered, and a Reaction Talent offered in the Combat window is not a row of the tab.
  • Sight is read, hearing is not. SEEN is line of sight between token centres against sight-blocking walls plus three statuses; light, sight range and hearing are the table's. [REQUIRES foe in sight] (0.29.0) is the same reading, asked by the Maneuvers tab of every other token on the scene.
  • A loaded weapon is the weapon's own count, and nothing refuses an empty one (0.29.0). The loaded and unloaded words read the count on the weapon in hand: a Strike with it in an encounter uses a shot, the Reload Maneuver fills it for that weapon's Reload cost, and the chip on its Equipment row corrects it by hand. A Strike with an empty weapon still happens and its card says so. Outside an encounter nothing is counted. Ammunition itself (arrows, bolts) is not counted yet.
  • An Effect is read where it stands (0.31.0; rulings 305 to 310). IF: EFFECT(<name>) asks the creature rolling, and a bonus that waits on it is in the sheet's Threshold for as long as the Effect is on: put Taking Cover on and Guard moves on the sheet. IFT: EFFECT(<name>) asks the roll's other party, so it is read only where there is one: the Combat window's preview, the card, a Strike's pairing with each defender (never the blind attack die), a Defense roll, and a check read against one creature's Threshold. An adversary's Effects are read as a character's are. A [REQUIRES effect ...] block and a with are read by the Maneuvers tab, which looks again whenever an effect on any creature changes (a custom effect row on ANOTHER character is the one change it does not hear until something else moves). A named Effect is put on by a Maneuver's APPLY (below) or by a hand: the Effects tab's Active Effects, where a player's change is said in chat (a custom effect row's label is not: the row is the player's own, as its lines are). The hover card lists a creature's hand-made Effects for its owner and the GM, and an applied one for everyone. Where one Talent has a line on the attack die and another line that waits on the defender (ATK: 1 and ATK: 2; IFT: EFFECT(prone)), the two are one circumstance, counted once: +2 against a Prone defender, not +3.
  • A Maneuver puts Effects on, and takes them off (0.32.0; rulings 311 to 321; section 4, apply). An APPLY or REMOVE line on a Maneuver's own row acts when the Maneuver is used from its row: with no IF: RESULT, as the cost is paid, on the Maneuver's own card; with one, after the check, on the creature using it at once and on the creature targeted by the button on the card ("Apply to Bandit: Prone"), which the roller's owner or the GM presses once. The client that writes a target is the GM's, or its owner's with no GM; with neither connected the presser is told and nothing lands. An IMMUNE line stops a Condition as it stops one from the token palette. A Condition already on by other means is left alone. A window (UNTIL:) is counted in the encounter the Effect was applied in and closes on the turn change it names; the Effect goes then with no card, and every window ends with the encounter. Outside an encounter a line with a window is not applied. EFFECT(<name>, mine) on a bonus line holds only for an Effect the creature rolling applied. Nothing is applied by a Maneuver the system runs another way (a Strike, a Rush's drag), by an adversary's roll, from a blind roll by itself, or by a check that had no Threshold.
  • Nothing reads a Talent's Effect text. What the cell does not say, the system does not do: every clause with no line for it is the table's.
  • Adversaries. A rule on an adversary's Item is indexed but no adversary roll asks for modifiers (adversaries roll flat), and no adversary casts. A prevent on an adversary works, since Conditions are set on adversaries as on characters.

"<words>": a Bind's state is neutral, controlling, controlled, as in `bind, neutral`a word after bind that is no state (0.31.0)

"<name>" cannot be an Effect's name: ...a name that is a word of the grammar (or, not, self, target, none, a dash), that holds or or and as a word, or that has a character other than letters, digits, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes (0.31.0)
"<words>": an Exposed Zone is read off the Zone, not as an Effect; no line reads it yeteffect exposed head, EFFECT(exposed) (0.31.0)

A row's lines act for whoever has the Condition, a character or an adversary. So a row reads the four modifier tags and nothing that asks about an owner:

[EFFECT DEF: -2 situation, evade]              Off-Guard
[EFFECT DEF: -N condition]                     Frightened: all four Defenses, at its value
[EFFECT CHECK: -N condition]                   ... every check, and an Initiative rolled as one
[EFFECT ATK: -N condition]                     ... every Strike and Cast
[EFFECT DEF: 2 situation, evade; IFT: RANGED]  Prone: +2 Evade against a ranged Attack
  • **N is the Condition's own value.** -N on Frightened is -2 at Frightened 2 and -3 at Frightened 3. It is read only on a row whose Takes is N; on a Talent or a Maneuver, or on a row that takes no value, it is refused and a whole number is asked for. N with no sign is a bonus of the value.
  • **After IFT: a row may ask about the attack it answers**: BLOW, BLAST, BLIGHT, BEGUILEMENT, MELEE, RANGED, TRAIT(<Trait>). Such a line is read where the attack is known (the Defense roll, the Threshold an attack is read against) and is not in the number on the sheet.

What a Condition forbids (movement, Reactions, a Defense) and how it fades have no word yet.
  • One Condition is one circumstance. A creature that is Off-Guard three ways (the status, Prone, a Torso Wound) takes Off-Guard's -2 once.
  • A Condition's lines have no On / Skip / Off. The Condition is the switch: take it off and its lines go. The Effects tab lists them under the Condition's row, read-only.

REMOVE: off-guard does not stand a Prone creature up: Prone is what holds the Off-Guard, and the Off-Guard goes when Prone does.

The row is the word (ruling 329). A row whose Automation cell is blank or N/A means the Condition changes no number, even Off-Guard, Frightened and Fatigued, whose numbers were in the system's code before the workbook. Two Conditions are two circumstances. A creature that is both Prone and Supine takes the lines of both (-2 to attacks twice); Drop Prone and Drop Supine each take the other off, so a Maneuver never leaves both.

Adversaries. A Condition's lines move an adversary's numbers as they move a character's (ruling 324): its Defense Thresholds, its Attack Thresholds, its own attack die, its Initiative. Its sheet shows the number the GM typed, which is what the field edits, and the number in effect beside it while a Condition moves it. An adversary's own Talents are still unread.
